title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Has the meaning given in the ASX Listing Rules: persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, directly or indirectly, including any director, and any Premier or Group employees with regular access to confidential financial information as specified by the CEO or Chairman.

tiers.name: Chief Executive Officer
tiers.description: Premier's Chief Executive Officer; distinguished only for the pre-dealing notification, which is given to the Chairman instead of the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman of Premier; distinguished only for the identity of the Designated Officer who considers their exceptional-circumstances application to deal during a Prohibited Period (the Managing Director, instead of the Chairman).

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A person who the Key Management Person proposes to act in concert with, formally or informally, including family members and entities such as companies and trusts controlled by the Key Management Person.

windows.start_anchor: the release of the Company's half year results to the ASX
the release of the Company's preliminary final report to the ASX
commencement of the rights trading period when the Company has issued a prospectus for those rights
windows.end_anchor: end of that rights trading period

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board has discretion to prohibit trading by any Key Management Person during any additional periods when Premier is considering matters subject to the exceptions to the continuous disclosure requirements in Listing Rule 3.1A (clause 5); together with the window-based Closed Periods these form the 'Prohibited Period'. The Policy does not state whether such additional prohibitions are confidential.

rules.detail: Securities includes 'any derivatives including but not limited to options' with no venue limitation, and dealing includes the grant, acceptance, acquisition, disposal, exercise or discharge of any option or other right to acquire or dispose of securities. An OTC put/call is therefore a dealing requiring the standard pre-dealing notice and 14-day completion, confined to a window period or an approved exceptional dealing.
rules.evidence: any derivatives including but not limited to options in respect of any of (a) to (e) above.

rules.detail: The Policy contains no clause naming hedging and has no vesting-based or holding-lock restriction on hedging (unlike many peer policies). A hedge instrument over Premier securities is still caught only because it is a derivative security and a dealing under clause 10, so it requires the ordinary pre-dealing notice within a window period.
rules.evidence: 'dealing' includes: (a) any application for acquisition or disposal of any securities; (b) entering into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of any securities; and (c) the grant, acceptance, acquisition, disposal, exercise or discharge of any option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures (e.g. a prepaid forward) are not named; they are caught as an agreement to dispose of securities and require the standard pre-dealing notice within a window period.
rules.evidence: entering into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of any securities

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not named. A CFD referencing Premier shares is a derivative and so a security/dealing under clause 10, requiring the standard pre-dealing notice within a window period.
rules.evidence: any derivatives including but not limited to options in respect of any of (a) to (e) above.

rules.detail: Unlike most peer policies, margin lending is not named or prohibited anywhere in this Policy. Clause 4.1(f) tacitly acknowledges secured lending arrangements over Premier securities exist ('a loan agreement'), which would include a margin loan; only the resulting disposal, if it falls in a Closed Period, needs the Board's discretion to be permitted.
rules.evidence: a disposal of Premier's securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan agreement

rules.detail: Granting a charge, lien or pledge over Premier securities is not named, and 'dealing' does not expressly extend to encumbrance.

There is no clause banning secured financing arrangements over Premier securities. Clause 4.1(f) expressly contemplates 'a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan agreement' as a legitimate circumstance, subject only to the Board's discretion to allow the resulting disposal if it falls within a Closed Period.
rules.evidence: a disposal of Premier's securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan agreement

rules.detail: The Notice of Intention to Trade and the Application to Trade During a Prohibited Period each require the Key Management Person to represent that, if purchasing, they do not intend to sell the securities within 6 months of purchase. This applies to new purchases, not to disposals of, or hedges over, already-held vested securities.
rules.evidence: If I am purchasing securities, I do not intend to sell the securities within 6 months of the date of purchase.

clearance.evidence: they may notify the Company Secretary of their intention to deal in the Company's securities... No dealing may be undertaken before the notice has been received by the Company Secretary. The dealing must be completed within 14 days from the date that the notice is received by the Company Secretary, or such other time as is specified by the Designated Officer.
in the case of the Chief Executive Officer, he or she may notify the Chairman

short_term.evidence: If I am purchasing securities, I do not intend to sell the securities within 6 months of the date of purchase.

exceptions.evidence: whether the Applicant is suffering severe and unforeseen financial hardship
whether the Applicant is suffering severe and unforeseen health issues
whether the Applicant is bound by a court order, enforceable undertaking, or other legal or regulatory requirement to transfer or sell the securities of Premier
transfers of securities of the entity already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Key Management Person is a beneficiary

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of Premier) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

where a Key Management Person is a trustee, trading in the securities of Premier by that trust provided the Key Management Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Key Management Person
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, security purchase plan, dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.
a disposal of Premier's securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan agreement

the exercise (but not the sale of securities following the exercise) of an option or right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right, or the conversion of the security, falls during a Prohibited Period and Premier has been in an exceptionally long Prohibited Period

external_documents: Agreements between Premier and a Shareholder governing or restricting trading of shares
exemption_authority: The Designated Officer (the Chairman, or the Managing Director where the Chairman is the Applicant) may grant written permission to deal during a Prohibited Period in exceptional circumstances (severe and unforeseen financial hardship, severe and unforeseen health issues, a court order or enforceable undertaking, or other exceptional circumstances where the dealing is the only reasonable course of action), provided the Applicant is not in possession of inside information. Separately, the Board has discretion to lift the Closed Period restriction for the specific circumstances listed in clause 4.1, including a secured lender's forced sale under a loan agreement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy contains no clause prohibiting hedging of Company securities, margin lending, or secured financing arrangements generally.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no express bar on granting security over vested Premier shares to fund a collar loan; the only relevant control is that a secured lender's forced sale during a Closed Period requires the Board to exercise its discretion to lift the restriction (clause 4.1(f)).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where the provisions of an agreement between Premier and a Shareholder conflict with the provisions of this policy, the most restrictive provisions will prevail.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any separate restriction in the executive's employee share plan or personal agreement with Premier overrides this Policy if stricter, so those documents must be checked before relying on the absence of an express hedging or margin-lending ban here.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If I am purchasing securities, I do not intend to sell the securities within 6 months of the date of purchase.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This representation on the standard dealing forms is a de facto 6-month restriction on new purchases (longer than the usual 3-month rule), but it does not restrict hedging, encumbering or selling already-held vested shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: they may notify the Company Secretary of their intention to deal in the Company's securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routine dealing outside Prohibited Periods proceeds by notice, not a refusable approval, so a KMP without inside information has a comparatively low-friction path to executing a collar within a window period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Premier's securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This clause tacitly acknowledges that a KMP may grant security over Premier shares under a loan agreement; a bank's enforcement sale on default is contemplated by the Policy, subject to the Board exercising discretion to permit that sale if it falls within a Closed Period.

summary: A funded collar over Premier shares faces a comparatively light regime: this Policy has no hedging, margin lending or secured financing prohibition, and clause 4.1(f) expressly contemplates a secured lender exercising rights under a loan agreement, so the loan leg secured on vested shares is not itself restricted. The put/call derivative legs are 'securities'/'dealing' under the broad definitions (any derivatives, including options, and any agreement to acquire or dispose) and so require only a written pre-dealing notice to the Company Secretary (or, for the CEO, initial notice to the Chairman), completion within 14 days of the notice being received, and execution within a window period (six weeks after half-year or full-year results, or a rights trading period) or under a Designated Officer's exceptional-circumstances approval, never while holding inside information. A standard representation on the dealing forms states an intention not to sell newly purchased securities within 6 months, but this does not constrain hedging or encumbering already-held vested shares. If the bank needs to force a sale on default and that falls within a Closed Period, the Board must exercise its clause 4.1(f) discretion to permit it. Overall verdict: a funded collar is achievable with routine notice-based clearance in a window period, and the loan leg is not itself prohibited, making this one of the more collar-friendly policies, subject to checking the executive's own employee share plan or shareholder agreement for a stricter overriding term.
